explanation: Compared with Bonato–Janssen–Roshanbin (arXiv:1507.06524) and Norin–Turcotte (arXiv:2207.04035): every connected graph of order n has b(G) ≤ ⌈√n⌉. burningNumber is defined via the ball-cover characterisation of BJR16 (Corollary 3): sources x_0..x_{k-1} with every vertex within distance k-1-i of x_i (dist + i < k, with reachability making dist meaningful). The least such k is the burning number; allowing repeated/already-burnt sources does not change the minimum, as the docstring notes. Conclusion ≤ ⌈√(card V)⌉₊ with V finite and G connected. Faithful.
